title_en: How The Airbus A350 Survives Environmental Stress During The Longest Flights In The World
title_zh: 空客 A350 如何在世界上最长的飞行中承受环境压力
summary: A350's intensive certification campaign included specialized environmental testing and set an industry record for time to completion.
summary_zh: A350 的密集认证活动包括专门的环境测试，并创下了完成时间的行业记录。
body_en: With a Master’s degree in Air Transport Management, Viviana brings her passion for aviation to Simple Flying, while specialising in managing Time-Critical Aircraft on Ground (AOG) situations.

Before entering commercial service, the Airbus A350 had to prove it could withstand some of the harshest conditions on Earth. Airbus needed to establish how its engines, systems, and structure would respond to extreme temperatures and demanding operating conditions. From the freezing Canadian Arctic to the scorching deserts of the United Arab Emirates and the high-altitude airports of Bolivia, Airbus deliberately pushed its new widebody aircraft to its limits.

Through these trials, Airbus sought to ensure that the A350 could operate safely and reliably across a wide range of environments. The A350 has since become a key aircraft for ultra-long-haul operations, including Singapore Airlines ' nonstop flights between Singapore and New York. So, how did Airbus test the A350, and what did these trials reveal about the aircraft's capabilities?
The A350 Completed Its Certification Campaign In Just 14 Months

Before entering commercial service, every new aircraft must undergo extensive testing and certification to demonstrate compliance with aviation safety standards. For Airbus aircraft, the main certification authority is the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA), while the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) validates the design for the US market. The process begins with the Type Certificate (TC), which confirms that an aircraft's design meets the applicable airworthiness requirements. Manufacturers must also hold the relevant production approvals, while each individual aircraft requires a Certificate of Airworthiness (CoA) before entering service. Airlines must additionally meet operational requirements, including crew training, maintenance arrangements, and any necessary authorizations.

The certification process also varies depending on the aircraft's design and available configurations. For example, Airbus' A320neo Family certification program covered six airframe and engine combinations. The A319neo, A320neo and A321neo each required validation of their airframes, systems and two available engine options: the CFM International LEAP-1A and Pratt & Whitney Geared Turbofan (GTF). These campaigns also verified whether the aircraft met their performance targets for fuel consumption and range, reflecting improvements from the new engines and Sharklet wingtip devices.

For the A350-900, Airbus completed its flight-test and certification campaign in just over 14 months, setting an industry record for the program's completion time. Five test aircraft accumulated more than 2,600 flight hours, during which Airbus evaluated the aircraft's handling characteristics, systems, performance, and reliability. The campaign culminated in the A350-900 receiving Type Certification from EASA and the FAA in 2014. However, the program also involved specialized environmental testing in Canada, the United Arab Emirates, and Bolivia, along with controlled temperature trials at the McKinley Climatic Laboratory in the United States. These tests would establish how the A350 performed in conditions far beyond those encountered during routine airline operations.
How Airbus Tested The A350 In Temperatures As Low As -40°C

In January 2014, Airbus took its A350-900 MSN3 development aircraft to Iqaluit, Canada , to conduct cold-weather trials in temperatures as low as -28°C. A team of 48 Airbus specialists assessed how the aircraft's engines and systems performed in freezing conditions. One key test involved starting the engines and auxiliary power unit (APU) after a cold soak , during which the aircraft was left exposed to extremely low temperatures for an extended period. The team also conducted system checks, low-speed taxiing, rejected takeoffs, and a local test flight to verify the aircraft's performance.

Three years later, Airbus returned to Iqaluit with the larger A350-1000 , which underwent five days of intensive ground and flight testing in temperatures ranging from -28°C to -37°C. Alongside these Arctic trials, Airbus also used the McKinley Climatic Laboratory at Eglin Air Force Base in Florida, becoming the first Airbus aircraft to undergo testing at the facility. Unlike Iqaluit, where engineers depended on natural weather, the laboratory's climate-controlled hangar allowed Airbus to simulate temperatures from -40°C to +40°C under controlled conditions.

However, extreme cold was only one part of the A350's environmental testing program. While the Canadian trials focused on the aircraft's ability to operate in freezing conditions, Airbus also needed to assess its performance in extreme heat and at high-altitude airports. This took the A350 to Al Ain in the United Arab Emirates and La Paz in Bolivia, where high temperatures and reduced air density presented a different set of operational challenges.

While freezing temperatures presented one challenge, Airbus also needed to demonstrate that the A350 could operate safely in extreme heat. In July 2017, the manufacturer sent its A350-1000 test aircraft, MSN065, to Al Ain International Airport in the United Arab Emirates for a three-day hot-weather testing campaign. Conducted between 4 and 7 July, the trials exposed the aircraft to temperatures exceeding 40°C, reaching as high as 48°C. The objective was to assess how the aircraft's systems performed in scorching conditions, particularly the Rolls-Royce Trent XWB engines and cabin air-conditioning systems.

One main concern was whether the aircraft could maintain comfortable cabin temperatures on the ground, where cooling systems must cope with intense external heat. Engineers also assessed engine performance, as higher temperatures reduce air density and affect engine thrust and takeoff performance. This can increase the runway distance required for departure, particularly at airports with shorter runways. The importance of these limitations became evident in June 2017 , when extreme temperatures in Phoenix, Arizona, led to dozens of flight cancellations involving regional aircraft with lower maximum operating temperature limits.

According to Airbus, the A350-1000 successfully met all the parameters established for its Al Ain campaign, demonstrating its readiness to operate in extreme heat. However, high temperatures are not the only factor that reduces air density. Airports situated thousands of meters above sea level present similar performance challenges, even when outside temperatures are considerably lower. To assess these conditions, Airbus also conducted high-altitude testing in Bolivia.
body_zh: Viviana 拥有航空运输管理硕士学位，她将自己对航空的热情融入到 Simple Flying 中，同时专门负责管理时间紧迫的飞机地面 (AOG) 情况。
在进入商业服务之前，空客 A350 必须证明其能够承受地球上一些最恶劣的条件。空中客车公司需要确定其发动机、系统和结构如何应对极端温度和苛刻的操作条件。从寒冷的加拿大北极地区到阿拉伯联合酋长国的灼热沙漠和玻利维亚的高海拔机场，空中客车公司刻意将其新型宽体飞机推向极限。
通过这些试验，空中客车公司力求确保 A350 能够在各种环境下安全可靠地运行。此后，A350 成为超远程运营的关键飞机，包括新加坡航空在新加坡和纽约之间的直飞航班。那么，空中客车公司是如何测试 A350 的，这些测试揭示了该飞机的哪些能力呢？
A350仅用14个月就完成了认证活动

在进入商业服务之前，每架新飞机都必须经过广泛的测试和认证，以证明符合航空安全标准。对于空客飞机，主要认证机构是欧盟航空安全局 (EASA)，而美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 则针对美国市场验证设计。该过程从型号证书 (TC) 开始，该证书确认飞机的设计满足适用的适航要求。制造商还必须持有相关的生产批准，而每架飞机在投入使用之前都需要获得适航证书（CoA）。航空公司还必须满足运营要求，包括机组人员培训、维护安排和任何必要的授权。

认证过程也因飞机的设计和可用配置而异。例如，空中客车公司的 A320neo 系列认证计划涵盖六种机身和发动机组合。 A319neo、A320neo 和 A321neo 均需要验证其机身、系统和两种可用的发动机选项：CFM International LEAP-1A 和普惠齿轮涡轮风扇发动机 (GTF)。这些活动还验证了飞机是否达到了燃油消耗和航程的性能目标，反映出新发动机和 Sharklet 翼尖装置的改进。

对于 A350-900，空中客车公司仅用了 14 个多月的时间就完成了飞行测试和认证活动，创下了该项目完成时间的行业记录。五架测试飞机累计飞行超过 2,600 小时，期间空客评估了飞机的操纵特性、系统、性能和可靠性。该活动的高潮是 A350-900 于 2014 年获得了欧洲航空安全局 (EASA) 和美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 的型式认证。不过，该计划还涉及在加拿大、阿拉伯联合酋长国和玻利维亚进行的专门环境测试，以及在美国麦金利气候实验室进行的受控温度试验。这些测试将确定 A350 在远远超出常规航空公司运营时遇到的条件下的表现。
空客如何在低至 -40°C 的温度下测试 A350
2014年1月，空中客车公司将其A350-900 MSN3开发机带到加拿大伊卡卢伊特，在低至-28°C的温度下进行寒冷天气试验。由 48 名空客专家组成的团队评估了飞机发动机和系统在冰冻条件下的性能。一项关键测试涉及冷浸后启动发动机和辅助动力装置（APU），在此期间，飞机长时间暴露在极低的温度下。该团队还进行了系统检查、低速滑行、中断起飞和本地试飞，以验证飞机的性能。
三年后，空中客车公司带着更大的 A350-1000 重返伊魁特，该飞机在 -28°C 至 -37°C 的温度范围内进行了五天的密集地面和飞行测试。除了这些北极试验外，空客还使用了佛罗里达州埃格林空军基地的麦金利气候实验室，成为第一架在该设施接受测试的空客飞机。与工程师依赖自然天气的伊魁特实验室不同，该实验室的气候控制机库允许空中客车公司在受控条件下模拟 -40°C 至 +40°C 的温度。
然而，极寒只是 A350 环境测试计划的一部分。虽然加拿大的试验重点是飞机在冰冻条件下运行的能力，但空中客车公司还需要评估其在极热和高海拔机场的性能。 A350 飞往阿拉伯联合酋长国的艾恩和玻利维亚的拉巴斯，那里的高温和空气密度降低带来了一系列不同的运营挑战。

虽然冰冻温度是一项挑战，但空中客车公司还需要证明 A350 可以在极热条件下安全运行。 2017 年 7 月，该制造商将其 A350-1000 测试飞机 MSN065 送往阿拉伯联合酋长国艾恩国际机场，进行为期三天的炎热天气测试活动。试验于 7 月 4 日至 7 日期间进行，飞机暴露在超过 40°C 的温度下，最高可达 48°C。目的是评估飞机系统在炎热条件下的性能，特别是劳斯莱斯遄达 XWB 发动机和机舱空调系统。
一个主要问题是飞机是否能够在地面上保持舒适的机舱温度，因为冷却系统必须应对强烈的外部热量。工程师还评估了发动机性能，因为较高的温度会降低空气密度并影响发动机推力和起飞性能。这可能会增加起飞所需的跑道距离，特别是在跑道较短的机场。这些限制的重要性在 2017 年 6 月变得显而易见，当时亚利桑那州凤凰城的极端气温导致数十个航班取消，涉及最高运行温度限制较低的支线飞机。
据空中客车公司称，A350-1000 成功满足了为其艾因战役制定的所有参数，表明其已做好在极热条件下运行的准备。然而，高温并不是降低空气密度的唯一因素。即使室外温度低得多，海拔数千米的机场也会面临类似的性能挑战。为了评估这些条件，空客还在玻利维亚进行了高海拔测试。

body_en: Belgium inaugurates Europe's largest satellite factory as Aerospacelab rebrands as Ectro - Aviation24.be
Home Space Ectro (Aerospacelab) Belgium inaugurates Europe’s largest satellite factory as Aerospacelab rebrands as Ectro

Belgian satellite manufacturer Aerospacelab officially inaugurated its new satellite manufacturing megafactory in Marcinelle, near Charleroi, on 24 November, in the presence of King Philippe. The company also announced that it will change its name to Ectro from 30 November, marking a new chapter in its expansion into the European space industry.

The 20,000-square-metre facility represents an investment of approximately €100 million and is designed to produce up to 500 satellites annually, making it Europe’s largest satellite manufacturing plant and the third largest worldwide. The site includes 7,000 square metres of production space and 4,000 square metres of cleanroom facilities. Initial satellite production is expected to begin in January or February 2027, with operations gradually expanding thereafter.

The factory will play a major role in the European Union’s IRIS² secure satellite communications programme. In September, Aerospacelab secured a contract worth approximately €2.4 billion to manufacture 264 satellite platforms for the European constellation. IRIS² is intended to provide secure communications for European governments, institutions and commercial users, strengthening Europe’s strategic independence in satellite communications. The first satellites are expected to be launched from 2029.

Founded in 2018 by Benoît Deper, Aerospacelab has grown into one of Europe’s emerging satellite manufacturers. The new facility is expected to employ around 500 people initially, with the company aiming to reach approximately 1,000 employees by the end of 2027.

The new name, Ectro, is derived from the scientific concept of ectropy, referring to the increase of order and organisation within a system. According to CEO Benoît Deper, the rebranding also reflects the company’s transformation from a relatively small laboratory-style operation into a major industrial player. The new identity will officially take effect on 30 November.

The inauguration represents a significant milestone for Belgium’s aerospace industry and strengthens Europe’s ambitions to develop its own satellite manufacturing capabilities and reduce its dependence on foreign space infrastructure.

比利时 Ectro (Aerospacelab) 欧洲最大卫星工厂落成，Aerospacelab 更名为 Ectro
11 月 24 日，比利时卫星制造商 Aerospacelab 在沙勒罗瓦附近的 Marcinelle 正式启用了其新的卫星制造巨型工厂，菲利普国王出席了仪式。该公司还宣布将于11月30日起更名为Ectro，标志着其向欧洲航天工业扩张的新篇章。
该工厂占地 20,000 平方米，投资约 1 亿欧元，设计年产量高达 500 颗卫星，使其成为欧洲最大、全球第三大卫星制造工厂。该工厂包括 7,000 平方米的生产空间和 4,000 平方米的洁净室设施。最初的卫星生产预计将于 2027 年 1 月或 2 月开始，此后运营逐步扩大。
该工厂将在欧盟 IRIS² 安全卫星通信计划中发挥重要作用。 9 月，Aerospacelab 获得了一份价值约 24 亿欧元的合同，为欧洲星座制造 264 个卫星平台。 IRIS²旨在为欧洲政府、机构和商业用户提供安全通信，加强欧洲在卫星通信方面的战略独立性。第一批卫星预计将于 2029 年发射。
Aerospacelab 由 Benoît Deper 于 2018 年创立，现已发展成为欧洲新兴卫星制造商之一。新工厂最初预计将雇用约 500 名员工，公司的目标是到 2027 年底雇用约 1,000 名员工。
新名称 Ectro 源自科学概念“熵”，指的是系统内秩序和组织的增加。首席执行官伯努瓦·德佩尔 (Benoît Deper) 表示，品牌更名也反映出该公司从一家相对较小的实验室式企业转变为一家主要的工业企业。新身份将于11月30日正式生效。
此次落成是比利时航空航天业的一个重要里程碑，增强了欧洲发展自己的卫星制造能力并减少对外国太空基础设施依赖的雄心。

title_en: BermudAir Adding Flights All Over The Place: I Don’t Know What’s Going On
title_zh: 百慕大航空在各地增加航班：我不知道发生了什么
summary: BermudAir has announced a huge summer 2027 expansion, adding seasonal routes from Fredericton to Bermuda and from Nashville to Ocho Rios. The airline's strategy is increasingly hard to figure out.
summary_zh: 百慕大航空宣布 2027 年夏季进行大规模扩张，增加从弗雷德里克顿飞往百慕大以及从纳什维尔飞往奥乔里奥斯的季节性航线。航空公司'
body_en: BermudAir, the unusual boutique carrier that launched operations a few years back, keeps getting stranger. The company has just announced a massive expansion for the summer of 2027, and with this, we’ll see the airline add all kinds of seemingly random routes to and from Bermuda, plus all kinds of routes that don’t touch Bermuda.
Whether you want to fly from Nashville to Ocho Rios, or from Fredericton to Bermuda, the airline now has you covered!
BermudAir adds flights all over the place (don’t ask me!)

For a little bit of background, in mid-2023 we saw the launch of BermudAir , a quirky niche airline with the goal of operating Embraer jets between Bermuda (BDA) and the United States and Canada. Initially the airline was going to operate all-business class planes, but it scrapped (“delayed”) that concept before launch , instead introducing a two-cabin concept (though business class just has blocked adjacent seats and better service).
As I said from the beginning, the whole thing struck me as an odd venture, essentially trying to serve Bermuda year-round profitably, while going up against the major carriers that serve the airport.

To my surprise, the airline is still in business over three years after launch, though it hasn’t necessarily been that smooth. As is pretty common for an airlines startup, the first years have been rocky, with several routes being cut after launch. For that matter, the airline faced a lawsuit over millions in unpaid airport fees at its hub, which isn’t exactly a great sign.

Several months back, BermudAir announced new winter 2026-2027 seasonal flying to places other than Bermuda. Now the airline has announced summer seasonal flying for 2027, and it’s arguably even stranger. The routes are all over the place.

On top of that, the airline will be expanding beyond Bermuda, with new seasonal services in the following markets
Between Baltimore (BWI) and Guatemala City (GUA) and San Salvador (SAL)
Between Fort Lauderdale (FLL) and Grand Cayman (GCM)
Between Nashville (BNA) and Grand Cayman (GCM) and Ocho Rios (OCJ)
Between New Orleans (MSY) and Grand Cayman (GCM), Ocho Rios (OCJ), Providenciales (PLS), and San Pedro Sula (SAP)
Between Orlando Sanford (SFB) and Ocho Rios (OCJ)
Between Raleigh Durham (RDU) and Ocho Rios (OCJ)
Between San Antonio (SAT) and Belize (BZE) and Grand Cayman (GCM)

无论您是想从 纳什维尔 飞往 奥乔里奥斯，还是从 弗雷德里克顿 飞往 百慕大，该航空公司现在都能满足您的需求！
百慕大航空在各地增加航班（别问我！）
作为一点背景知识，我们在 2023 年中期看到了百慕大航空 (BermudAir) 的成立，这是一家奇特的利基航空公司，其目标是在百慕大 (BDA) 与美国和加拿大之间运营巴西航空工业公司 (Embraer) 喷气式飞机。最初，该航空公司打算运营全商务舱飞机，但在推出之前放弃（“推迟”）了这一概念，而是引入了两舱概念（尽管商务舱只是封锁了相邻的座位和更好的服务）。
正如我从一开始就说过的，整件事让我觉得这是一次奇怪的冒险，本质上是试图为百慕大提供全年盈利的服务，同时与为机场提供服务的主要航空公司竞争。
令我惊讶的是，该航空公司在成立三年多后仍在运营，尽管并不一定那么顺利。对于航空公司初创公司来说，最初的几年并不顺利，几条航线在推出后被削减，这是很常见的。就此而言，该航空公司面临着针对其枢纽机场数百万美元未付机场费用的诉讼，这并不是一个好兆头。
